 YouTube Issues Are Mostly Resolved: What to Know
 Over 24,000 YouTube users reported issues with the platform on Wednesday morning.
 Katelyn Chedraoui 
 Reporter 2
 Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators.… Read full bio 
 Katelyn Chedraoui
 Reporter 2
 Read full bio 
 Edited by Jon Reed 
 October 28, 2026, 1:16 pm ET
 1 min read 
 Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto/Getty Images 
 If you had problems streaming videos on YouTube on Wednesday, you weren’t alone. Over 24,000 YouTube users have reported issues with the video-streaming platform, according to DownDetector.
 Outage reports peaked shortly after 9 a.m. ET but have declined in the hours since then. Most of the reports said people were struggling to stream video. YouTube confirmed those issues in a support page , saying that users were encountering “video unavailable” messages, buffering or getting stuck in a loading loop and having their video player window blacked out. A YouTube spokesperson told CNET via email that they are aware of the issue and working on a fix.
 If YouTube is working for you, you can check out CNET’s livestream of us testing the iPhone Duo by folding it over 82,000 times so far.
 Oct 28, 2026 12:31 PM ET 
 YouTube service is mostly restored
 Katelyn Chedraoui 
 As of 12:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday, reports of YouTube outages have sharply fallen.
 Screenshot by Katelyn Chedraoui/CNET 
 Oct 28, 2026 11:04 AM ET 
 DownDetector reports spike
 Katelyn Chedraoui 
 Screenshot by Katelyn Chedraoui/CNET 
 DownDetector, a popular platform that tracks software outages, saw a sharp spike in reports after 9 a.m. ET on Wednesday. So far, over 24,000 YouTube users have reported issues with the platform.
